---
title: "Licensing Outreach"
subtitle: "Helping open source science tools get their licensing right"
---

Publishing source code is not the same as making it reusable. Without a clear and correct license, nobody has legal permission to use, modify, or redistribute the software, however openly it is shared. Many research tools are missing a license or use one that does not match how the software is actually meant to be used. This makes it harder to reuse them, often without the authors realising.

As part of the FAIRtools framework project, we reached out to developers of open source science tools directly. We opened **36 GitHub issues** that pointed out missing or incorrect licensing and explained why it matters for reuse, with practical suggestions for fixing it.

As a result, **4 tools** now have a correct software license, which makes them legally reusable by other researchers.
